neom.name: NEOM
neom.tagline: A land of the future, built from scratch.
neom.about: NEOM is a giga-project in Tabuk Province, northwest Saudi Arabia, on the Red Sea and the Gulf of Aqaba. It brings together new cities, ports, tourism destinations and nature reserves under one vision.

attractions.name: The Line
attractions.desc: A linear city with no cars or streets.

attractions.name: Oxagon
attractions.desc: A floating industrial port city.

attractions.name: Trojena
attractions.desc: A mountain destination with outdoor skiing.

attractions.name: Magna
attractions.desc: A coastal region along the Gulf of Aqaba.

attractions.name: NEOM Islands
attractions.desc: Luxury islands in the Red Sea, starting with Sindalah.

attractions.name: Nature in NEOM
attractions.desc: Protected reserves, deserts and coral reefs.

timeline.event: NEOM announced at the Future Investment Initiative.

red-sea.name: The Red Sea
red-sea.about: A regenerative tourism destination on Saudi Arabia's west coast, spread across islands, desert, volcanoes and coral reefs, developed by Red Sea Global.

attractions.name: Shura Island
attractions.desc: The main resort hub shaped like a dolphin.

attractions.name: Coral Reefs
attractions.desc: One of the world's richest reef systems.

attractions.name: Ummahat Islands
attractions.desc: Private island resorts over turquoise lagoons.

attractions.name: Mangroves
attractions.desc: Coastal forests protected and replanted.

timeline.event: First resorts and Red Sea International Airport opened.

qiddiya.name: Qiddiya
qiddiya.tagline: The capital of entertainment, sports and culture.
qiddiya.about: Qiddiya is a giga-project near Riyadh dedicated to entertainment, sports and culture, with theme parks, a motorsport track and a major stadium.

attractions.name: Six Flags Qiddiya
attractions.desc: A theme park with record-breaking rides.

attractions.name: Aquarabia
attractions.desc: A large water theme park.

attractions.name: Speed Park
attractions.desc: A motorsport track built into the cliffs.

attractions.name: Gaming & Esports District
attractions.desc: A hub for gaming and esports.

diriyah.name: Diriyah
diriyah.about: Diriyah, on the edge of Riyadh, was the first capital of the Saudi state. Its At-Turaif district is a UNESCO World Heritage Site, and the area is being developed into a cultural and lifestyle destination.

attractions.name: At-Turaif
attractions.desc: Historic mud-brick district and UNESCO site.

attractions.name: Bujairi Terrace
attractions.desc: Dining destination overlooking At-Turaif.

attractions.name: Wadi Hanifah
attractions.desc: A green valley running through Diriyah.

attractions.name: Saudi Heritage
attractions.desc: Traditional arts like the Ardah dance.

timeline.event: Diriyah becomes the capital of the first Saudi state.
At-Turaif listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

roshn.name: ROSHN
roshn.about: ROSHN is a national real estate developer owned by the Public Investment Fund, building integrated residential communities across the Kingdom.

attractions.name: SEDRA
attractions.desc: A green community in north Riyadh.

attractions.name: WAREFA
attractions.desc: A residential community in east Riyadh.

attractions.name: ALAROUS
attractions.desc: A coastal community in Jeddah.

attractions.name: MARAFY
attractions.desc: A waterfront community in north Jeddah.

timeline.event: ROSHN launched by the Public Investment Fund.
ROSHN becomes title sponsor of the Saudi Pro League.

alula.name: AlUla
alula.about: AlUla in northwest Saudi Arabia is home to thousands of years of history, from the Nabataean tombs of Hegra to dramatic desert landscapes, now developed as a global cultural destination.

attractions.name: Hegra
attractions.desc: Nabataean tombs carved into sandstone.

attractions.name: Desert Canyons
attractions.desc: Dramatic rock formations and valleys.

attractions.name: AlUla Oasis
attractions.desc: Palm groves along the ancient valley.

attractions.name: Sharaan Nature Reserve
attractions.desc: Home to the Arabian leopard program.

timeline.event: Hegra becomes Saudi Arabia's first UNESCO site.
